subject: ela
intro: Good readers ask and answer questions to understand informational text. We use question words — who, what, where, when, why, and how — to find key details in nonfiction passages. After asking a question, look back in the text for the specific words that answer it.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Owls are birds that hunt at night. They have large eyes that help them see in the dark. Owls use their sharp talons to catch mice and other small animals. Most owls live in forests and woodlands.

Where do most owls live?

steps: I ask myself: where is a place mentioned in this article?
I look for place words in the text.
I read: 'Most owls live in forests and woodlands.'
The place words are 'forests and woodlands.'
I point to that sentence in the text to support my answer.
So the answer is most owls live in forests and woodlands.
solution.answer: Most owls live in forests and woodlands.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The Amazon River is one of the longest rivers in the world. It flows through South America. The river is home to thousands of fish, including piranhas. People who live near the Amazon use the river for water and food.

Why do people who live near the Amazon use the river?

steps: I ask myself: why do people use the river?
I look for the sentence that explains the reason.
I read: 'People who live near the Amazon use the river for water and food.'
The words 'for water and food' tell me why.
So the answer is people use the Amazon River for water and food.
solution.answer: People who live near the Amazon use the river for water and food.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Volcanoes are mountains that can shoot out hot melted rock. The melted rock is called lava. When a volcano erupts, lava flows down its sides. Some volcanoes erupt every few years, while others have not erupted in thousands of years.

What is the melted rock that comes out of a volcano called?

steps: I ask myself: what is the name for the melted rock?
I look for a definition sentence.
I read: 'The melted rock is called lava.'
The word 'lava' is the answer.
So the answer is the melted rock is called lava.
solution.answer: The melted rock is called lava.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Honey bees are busy insects. Worker bees leave the hive each morning to collect nectar from flowers. They carry nectar back to the hive, where it is turned into honey. One hive can make over 60 pounds of honey in a single year.

When do worker bees leave the hive to collect nectar?

steps: I ask myself: when do worker bees leave?
I look for a time word in the sentence about leaving the hive.
I read: 'Worker bees leave the hive each morning to collect nectar from flowers.'
The time word is 'each morning.'
So the answer is worker bees leave the hive each morning.
solution.answer: Worker bees leave the hive each morning to collect nectar.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Glaciers are giant rivers of ice that move very slowly. They form in cold mountain regions where more snow falls than melts each year. Over time, the packed snow turns into thick ice. Glaciers carve out valleys as they slowly creep downhill.

How do glaciers form?

steps: I ask myself: how do glaciers form?
I look for sentences that describe what happens over time.
I read: 'They form in cold mountain regions where more snow falls than melts each year. Over time, the packed snow turns into thick ice.'
These two sentences explain the process.
So the answer is glaciers form when more snow falls than melts, and the packed snow slowly turns into thick ice.
solution.answer: Glaciers form when more snow falls than melts each year, and the packed snow turns into thick ice.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Cheetahs are the fastest land animals on Earth. They can run up to 70 miles per hour in short bursts. Cheetahs live on the grassy plains of Africa. They use their speed to chase and catch prey like gazelles.

Who are the fastest land animals on Earth?
items.hint: Look for the sentence that names the fastest land animal.

steps: I ask: who are the fastest land animals?
I read the first sentence: 'Cheetahs are the fastest land animals on Earth.'
The answer is right there.
So the answer is cheetahs are the fastest land animals on Earth.
solution.answer: Cheetahs are the fastest land animals on Earth.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The Great Wall of China is one of the longest structures ever built. Workers began building it more than 2,000 years ago. The wall stretches across mountains and valleys in northern China. It was built to protect China from invaders.

Why was the Great Wall of China built?
items.hint: Look for the sentence that explains the purpose of the wall.

steps: I ask: why was the wall built?
I look for a 'to' or 'because' phrase that gives a reason.
I read: 'It was built to protect China from invaders.'
The reason is 'to protect China from invaders.'
So the answer is the Great Wall was built to protect China from invaders.
solution.answer: The Great Wall of China was built to protect China from invaders.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Desert tortoises live in the hot, dry deserts of the American Southwest. During the hottest part of summer, they burrow underground to stay cool. They can store water inside their bodies for many months. Desert tortoises can live for more than 50 years.

How do desert tortoises stay cool in summer?
items.hint: Look for what desert tortoises do when it is very hot.

steps: I ask: how do desert tortoises stay cool?
I look for the sentence about what they do during the hottest part of summer.
I read: 'During the hottest part of summer, they burrow underground to stay cool.'
The action word is 'burrow underground.'
So the answer is desert tortoises burrow underground to stay cool.
solution.answer: Desert tortoises burrow underground to stay cool in summer.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Nurses work in hospitals, clinics, and schools. They take care of patients who are sick or hurt. Nurses check patients' temperatures, give medicine, and help doctors during treatment. They work hard to help people get better.

Where do nurses work?
items.hint: Look for place words in the first sentence.

steps: I ask: where do nurses work?
I read the first sentence: 'Nurses work in hospitals, clinics, and schools.'
The place words are 'hospitals, clinics, and schools.'
So the answer is nurses work in hospitals, clinics, and schools.
solution.answer: Nurses work in hospitals, clinics, and schools.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The water cycle moves water around Earth. Water evaporates from oceans and lakes and rises into the sky as water vapor. The vapor cools and forms clouds. Then water falls back to Earth as rain or snow.

What happens to water vapor when it cools?
items.hint: Look for the sentence about what water vapor does after it cools.

steps: I ask: what happens when water vapor cools?
I look for the sentence with the word 'cools.'
I read: 'The vapor cools and forms clouds.'
The answer is it forms clouds.
So the answer is when water vapor cools, it forms clouds.
solution.answer: When water vapor cools, it forms clouds.
